learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the general organization of the human body, including the main organs, systems, and their functional relationships.
Understand the fundamental principles of the major diagnostic imaging techniques and their applications in diagnostic pathways.
Relate anatomical knowledge to the representations obtained through different medical imaging modalities.
Recognize the potential, limitations, and fields of application of the principal diagnostic methodologies.
Use appropriate anatomical, technical, and scientific terminology.
Critically interpret scientific and technical information related to the topics covered during the course.
Demonstrate the basic knowledge required for subsequent courses in biomedical sciences and biomedical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Notions of physics of ionizing radiations
Overview of radiographic image formation mechanisms
Principles of diagnostics applied to the various organs and systems
Anatomical terminology; classification of body systems, organs, tissues and membranes; regions and cavities of the human body
Functional anatomy of the human body systems: musculoskeletal, circulatory, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, endocrine, integumentary and nervous systems, and sensory organs.

assessment_methods.method: Oral exam (Diagnostic Imaging and Radiotherapy Module)
Homework/thesis papers (Diagnostic Imaging and Radiotherapy Module)

assessment_rules: The overall evaluation of the Integrated Course is based on the marks from each module, with the Human Anatomy Module contributing 50% and the Diagnostic Imaging Module contributing 50%. For the Human Anatomy Module, students can take a written in-course examination (31 multiple-choice questions, 1 point per correct answer) or an oral examination (3-4 questions). Grades range from 18/30 to 30 cum laude, reflecting knowledge, application skills, terminology use, and ability to relate concepts. Erasmus students may request to take the exam in English.
